summary: MISSION: AFTERLIFE is an interactive digital storytelling project that explores NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. It turns forgotten spacecraft parts, rover components, landing systems and scientific instruments into educational stories that explain what each object was, how it worked, why it was left behind and what it taught us. Through an interactive map, photographs, mission timelines and simple explanations, students can explore these objects and understand the engineering behind space exploration. The project addresses NASA’s challenge by making the history of abandoned equipment more engaging, accessible and understandable for younger audiences. It is important because these objects are more than just discarded equipment; they are evidence of human curiosity, scientific progress and technological achievement. MISSION: AFTERLIFE gives these forgotten objects a second life by turning them into learning opportunities and inspiring the next generation of space explorers.
details:
MISSION: AFTERLIFE is an educational digital storytelling platform designed to help students discover the stories behind NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. It works by organising space equipment into interactive story cards, supported by photographs, mission timelines and simple explanations. Users can explore different objects, learn their original purpose, understand how they were used during missions and discover why they remained on the lunar or Martian surface.

The project benefits students, teachers and space enthusiasts by making complex scientific information easier to understand and more interesting. Its intended impact is to increase awareness of space exploration, encourage curiosity about science and technology, and show how even equipment left behind can continue teaching us valuable lessons.

The initial project was developed using Microsoft PowerPoint for the presentation and visual prototype, alongside AI-generated concept artwork. The proposed digital platform could be expanded using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with NASA’s publicly available images and mission information as research sources.

The creative aspect of MISSION: AFTERLIFE is that it transforms discarded equipment into individual stories rather than simply presenting a list of objects. We considered educational value, scientific accuracy, accessibility, visual design and age-appropriate explanations when developing the concept. Our goal is to make space history enjoyable and understandable while inspiring future generations to explore beyond Earth.
